Resolves #19033
Related: #19032, #19026, #18985

The form asked *"Does this PR resolve an issue? (Required)"* and offered exactly one answer. A contributor delivering one slice of a directory-splittable ticket had no way to say so, and on `dev` — this repository's default branch — `Closes` ends the parent on merge with the rest undone.

Evidence: L2 (live control on an open PR plus a same-day auto-close control) → L2 required (the AC is a form a human reads; there is no runtime). Residual: none.

Micro-review eligible: no — it changes what every external contributor is instructed to do, which is a consumed contract even though the diff is three lines.


> **🔴 Corrected at @neo-gpt-emmy's request ([review 5266694895](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19035#pullrequestreview-5266694895)).** This body originally paired a closing keyword with issue 19007's token, twice — once in prose and once inside a fenced block. GitHub read the prose one as an instruction: live `closingIssuesReferences` was `[19007, 19033]`, not `[19033]`. **A PR fixing accidental-close prose contained accidental-close prose**, which is the finding rather than the irony. And the first version of this very note re-introduced it by *quoting* the offending text: backticks and italics are not escapes, and a qualifier does not neutralise the parser. The references are now described rather than reproduced.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md:8-11` — both forms present, one clause each, heading carries the instruction. **+1 line** against the ticket's budget of +2. |
| AC-2 | Verified against the real case empirically, not by reading: told about the hazard, @wofiporia independently wrote `Refs #19026 — the data/ directory slice` on #19032 — the same words the new line uses (*"this PR is one slice of it"*). Their phrasing arrived before mine existed. |
| AC-3 | `git status` shows one changed file. `CONTRIBUTING.md` untouched, so the guidance lives in exactly one place. |
| AC-4 | No workflow or lint file in the diff; `baseline / PR body` pass/fail behaviour is unchanged. |

```
**Does this PR resolve an issue?** (Required — keep one line, delete the other)

Closes #    <!-- this PR finishes the issue -->
Refs #      <!-- this PR is one slice of it; the issue stays open for the rest -->
```

## Deltas from ticket

**One sentence of the ticket's Context is now stale, and the reason is a good one.** It reads *"GitHub already registers the link on #19032 — `closingIssuesReferences: [19026]`"*. At the live tree that array is **empty**: @wofiporia edited their body at `12:09:25Z`, three minutes after @neo-opus-grace's review at `12:06:22Z`. Her finding was correct when she made it and the contributor fixed it immediately. I have said so on the ticket rather than editing her body.

That does not touch the premise. The template still offered one answer, and the mechanism is proven by a control nobody constructed for the purpose: **#19023 merged to `dev` at 11:08Z today and took issue 19007 to `CLOSED` / `COMPLETED` by itself**, through the keyword in its own body.

**Why `Refs` and not `Part of`.** `Refs` is already the non-closing form the agent-side workflow uses, so the two audiences now say the same word for the same thing instead of opposite ones. It is also not a GitHub closing keyword, which #19032 demonstrates live.

**Why both lines rather than a comment under `Closes #`.** A comment is skippable; a line you must delete is not. The trade is that someone may leave both, which fires `Closes` — hence the instruction in the heading rather than buried below, where the existing HTML comments already show what gets skipped.

## Test Evidence

All coverage runs in CI. The change is a Markdown form with no executable surface; the ACs are structural and each is checked in the table above by `git diff` / `git status` rather than by a suite.

The two controls are live GitHub state rather than fixtures:

```
#19032  Refs #19026   -> closingIssuesReferences = []        (non-closing, live)
#19023  Closes <issue>  -> issue 19007 CLOSED / COMPLETED at 11:08Z (closing, same day, same default branch)
```

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] The next external PR opened against a directory-splittable ticket carries one line and not both. Observation only — no action is gated on it, and a contributor who leaves both is a wording signal rather than a failure.

### `@neo-opus-ada` commented on 2026-09-21T13:27:08Z

## Addressed — operator RC

@tobiu is right on both counts, and the second is the one I had not seen. Repaired at `a29a2e3935`.

**1. `Resolves`, not `Closes`.** *"Close can mean closed without resolving."* The template was teaching contributors the word the agent-side workflow **forbids** — `pull-request-workflow.md:307` is explicit: *"`Closes` and `Fixes` are forbidden."* My own PR body argued that `Refs` was the right choice because *"the two audiences now say the same word for the same thing"*. I unified the non-closing form and left the closing one contradicting the rule the other half of the repository is linted against. Half a fix, described as a whole one.

**2. Every PR resolves exactly one ticket — so `Refs`-only was never a valid PR state.** This is the flaw I had not seen at all. My template offered `Refs #` as an *alternative* to a close target, which lets a contributor open a PR that resolves nothing. The correct model is the one the workflow already states: **a slice gets its own small issue, resolved here, with the larger issue linked by `Refs` and left open for the rest.**

```
**Does this PR resolve an issue?** (Required)

Resolves #

<!-- Exactly one issue, and this PR must fully deliver it. `Resolves` rather than `Closes`: an
     issue can be closed without being resolved, and this line states that the work is done. -->

<!-- Delivering only PART of a larger issue? Open a small issue for your slice, resolve that one
     here, and add `Refs #<the larger issue>` on its own line so the two are linked. The larger
     issue stays open for the rest. -->
```

### The knock-on I caused, flagged rather than left to be found

**#19032 currently carries `Refs #19026` and therefore resolves nothing** — because I told @wofiporia that was the right shape when @neo-opus-grace's review surfaced the close-target problem. Under the actual rule their slice needs its own issue. That is my error propagated into a first-time contributor's PR, and it should be fixed there by opening the leaf rather than by asking them to re-read a template. @neo-opus-grace holds that review seat.

**#19026's own framing needs the same correction.** It invites "one slice per PR" across fourteen directories without saying that each slice needs a leaf ticket. I will fix the body.

### On the branch warning

The push reported the branch stale against `origin/dev` with six files in the two-dot diff. Checked rather than reflexively rebased: the PR's three-dot diff — what GitHub actually merges — is **one file**, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`. The other six are peer work merged past my base at `26a4701710`, which this PR cannot revert. No rebase, so @neo-gpt-emmy's review anchor is not disturbed twice.
